options_evaluated: Recycled-content monomaterial polypropylene (rPP) with structural ribbing
decisions.conflict: In-Service Agent recommends high-impact thick-walled virgin polymers for durability; Circularity Agent rejects this, recommending a monomaterial polymer to maximize recycling quality.
espr_constraint: ESPR 2024/1781 Annex I (a), page 79: durability and reliability of the product or its components
ESPR 2024/1781 Annex I (h), page 79: use or content of recycled materials
ESPR 2024/1781 Annex I (t), page 80: lightweight design through reduction of material consumption and load-optimisation
ESPR 2024/1781 Annex I (p), page 80: microplastic and nanoplastic release during relevant product life cycle stages
decisions.chief_resolution: Recycled-content monomaterial polypropylene (rPP) with structural ribbing. This balances durability requirements under ESPR Annex I (a) with recycled content under (h) and lightweight design under (t) by using structural ribbing to compensate for rPP's lower tensile strength.
decisions.design_action: Investigate the availability of high-purity recycled polypropylene streams and verify if their mechanical properties can meet the structural requirements of the housing when reinforced with ribbing.

options_evaluated: Permanent chemical adhesives or ultrasonic welding
Reversible mechanical fasteners (standardized screws and snap-fits)
Threaded fasteners with molded-in metal inserts
decisions.conflict: In-Service Agent recommends threaded fasteners with metal inserts to ensure robust repairability; Circularity Agent rejects this because molded-in metal inserts contaminate the plastic recycling stream, hindering high-purity material recovery.
espr_constraint: ESPR 2024/1781 Annex I (b), page 79: ease of repair and maintenance, including ease of non-destructive disassembly
ESPR 2024/1781 Annex I (d), page 79: design for recycling, ease and quality of recycling, and high-purity sorting
ESPR 2024/1781 Annex I (e), page 79: avoidance of technical solutions detrimental to recycling of products and components
decisions.chief_resolution: Reversible mechanical fasteners (standardized screws and snap-fits) without molded-in metal inserts. This satisfies the ease of repair and maintenance under ESPR Annex I (b) while ensuring high-quality recycling and material recovery under (d) and (e) by avoiding inseparable metal-to-plastic joints.
decisions.design_action: Confirm the compatibility of standardized screw sizes across all internal components and investigate the feasibility of snap-fit geometries that can be disassembled using common household tools.

options_evaluated: High-efficiency brushless DC (BLDC) motor with rare-earth magnets
Modular brushless DC motor with easily removable magnets
decisions.conflict: Manufacture Agent recommends a synchronous reluctance motor to avoid the toxic emissions and energy-intensive extraction of rare-earth magnets; In-Service Agent recommends a high-efficiency brushless DC (BLDC) motor to maximize use-phase energy efficiency.
espr_constraint: ESPR 2024/1781 Annex I (g), page 79: use or consumption of energy, water and other resources in one or more life cycle stages
ESPR 2024/1781 Annex I (d), page 79: design for recycling, ease and quality of recycling
ESPR 2024/1781 Annex I (q), page 80: emissions to air, water or soil released in one or more lifecycle stages
decisions.chief_resolution: High-efficiency brushless DC (BLDC) motor designed with easily removable/separable rare-earth magnets and recycled copper windings. This prioritizes use-phase energy efficiency under ESPR Annex I (g) as a major environmental footprint driver, while satisfying circularity under (d) by ensuring the magnets can be easily extracted before shredding.
decisions.design_action: Investigate the supply chain viability for sourcing modular BLDC motors with magnetically separable rotors and verify the recycling efficiency of their rare-earth elements.

options_evaluated: Active cooling fan integrated into motor shaft
Oversized passive heat sinks with dedicated ventilation ducts
Removable/washable open-cell foam filters and heatsinks
decisions.conflict: Manufacture Agent recommends an active cooling fan integrated into the motor shaft to minimize manufacturing waste and material use; In-Service Agent recommends oversized passive heat sinks with dedicated ventilation ducts to eliminate moving parts and maximize reliability.
espr_constraint: ESPR 2024/1781 Annex I (a), page 79: durability and reliability of the product or its components
ESPR 2024/1781 Annex I (t), page 80: lightweight design through reduction of material consumption and load-optimisation
ESPR 2024/1781 Annex I (g), page 79: use or consumption of energy, water and other resources
decisions.chief_resolution: Passive cooling via optimized airflow channels using the vacuum's existing working airflow, combined with removable/washable filters and lightweight aluminum fins. This satisfies lightweight design under ESPR Annex I (t) by integrating functions (using working airflow for cooling) while avoiding the reliability risks of an active fan, thereby supporting durability under (a).
decisions.design_action: Investigate the thermal dissipation requirements of the selected motor and confirm whether the working airflow of the vacuum is sufficient to cool the motor under maximum load without active fans.

options_evaluated: Semi-modular design with standard fasteners for wear-and-tear parts
Highly modular architecture with toolless component swap
decisions.conflict: Manufacture Agent recommends a highly integrated monolithic design to simplify assembly and reduce production waste; Circularity Agent recommends a highly modular architecture with toolless component swap to facilitate repair, upgrading, and recycling.
espr_constraint: ESPR 2024/1781 Annex I (b), page 79: ease of repair and maintenance, modularity, and use of standard components
ESPR 2024/1781 Annex I (c), page 79: ease of upgrading, reuse, remanufacturing and refurbishment
ESPR 2024/1781 Annex I (j), page 80: weight and volume of the product and its packaging
decisions.chief_resolution: Semi-modular architecture with standardized fasteners for key functional blocks (motor, cord, filters). This balances ease of repair and maintenance under ESPR Annex I (b) with weight, volume, and material footprint constraints under (j) and (o) by avoiding the excessive material overhead of fully toolless modular connectors.
decisions.design_action: Investigate the optimal partitioning of functional modules (motor, cord, filter) to balance ease of repair with the complexity of internal electrical connections.

options_evaluated: Corded mains power with automatic cord reel
Corded mains power with manual cord wrap
Removable and standardized Li-ion battery pack
decisions.conflict: In-Service Agent recommends an automatic cord reel for user convenience and cable protection; Circularity Agent rejects this because the complex reel mechanism contains mixed materials (steel spring, copper contacts, plastic spool) that are difficult to disassemble and recycle.
espr_constraint: ESPR 2024/1781 Annex I (d), page 79: design for recycling, ease and quality of recycling
ESPR 2024/1781 Annex I (a), page 79: durability and reliability of the product or its components
ESPR 2024/1781 Annex I (r), page 80: amounts of waste generated, including plastic waste and packaging waste
decisions.chief_resolution: Corded mains power connection with a manual, integrated cord-wrap structure on the housing instead of an automatic mechanical cord reel. This eliminates hazardous battery waste under ESPR Annex I (r) and avoids the complex, unrecyclable mechanical reel mechanism to satisfy design for recycling under (d), while still providing cable management to protect the cord and maintain durability under (a).
decisions.design_action: Investigate user preferences regarding manual cord storage versus automatic reels, and verify the safety and regulatory standards for manual cord-wrap designs in the target markets.
